Class Extract

java.lang.Object
io.micronaut.runner.tools.Extract
public final class Extract extends Object
The extract mode: turns a runner jar into an ordinary Main-Class plus Class-Path layout that the JDK's own application class loader runs. 
java -Dmicronaut.runner.mode=extract -jar app.jar [--destination <dir>] [--force]

The result is a directory holding one jar per dependency under lib/ and the application's own jar beside them:

app/
  app.jar          the application layer, with Main-Class and Class-Path in its manifest
  lib/a.jar        the dependencies, byte for byte the nested jars the runner jar carries
  lib/b.jar

Why the mode exists

Nested mode loads application and dependency classes through RunnerClassLoader, which is a user-defined loader. HotSpot's AOT cache (JEP 483) refuses to link classes loaded by anything but a built-in loader, so the most valuable half of an AOT cache is out of reach of any single-file format, this one included. The extracted layout has no user-defined loader anywhere: every class comes from the JDK's application class loader, which is exactly the shape the AOT cache is built for. Nothing else about the application changes, because the jars under lib/ are the same bytes the runner jar carried.

What is left out of the application jar, and why

  • io/micronaut/runner/generated/** - the generated entry stub. It belongs to the runner format: it implements io.micronaut.runner.Entry and registers itself with Launcher, neither of which exists in the extracted layout. The manifest names the real application main class instead, so the stub would have no reader and could only fail to link.
  • the merged META-INF/micronaut/ copy at the archive root - the packager writes one merged, zero-length copy of every Micronaut service entry of the application and of every dependency into the outer root, so that the runner class loader can answer Micronaut's one directory listing from a single place. Under the JDK's loader that scan is a getResources walk over every jar on the class path, which finds each dependency's own entries inside its own jar under lib/ and the application's own entries inside the application jar. The merged copy would therefore duplicate all of them, and worse, it would make the application jar claim service entries that belong to dependencies: replacing one jar in lib/ would leave the application jar announcing a bean that the dependency no longer provides. So the merged copy is dropped. The application's own META-INF/micronaut/ entries survive, because they are physically part of the application layer (MICRONAUT-INF/classes/) and this mode copies the application layer, not the archive root.
  • MICRONAUT-INF/index.bin and io/micronaut/runner/*.class - the index and the launcher itself, for the same reason: they are the format, not the application.

The application jar's manifest

It is the application's own manifest (the attributes the packager recorded, per-package sections included) plus Main-Class, plus a Class-Path naming every dependency in index order - which is class path order, the order in which every lookup resolves - plus the Add-Opens, Add-Exports and Enable-Native-Access attributes the runner jar carried, plus Multi-Release when the application layer is multi-release. One consequence worth knowing: a dependency's own Class-Path attribute, which nested mode ignores, becomes active again here, because the JDK's loader honours it.

Safety

Everything is written into a temporary directory beside the destination and renamed into place, so an interrupted extraction leaves no half-written tree. A destination that already has anything in it is refused unless --force is given, a destination that contains the runner jar itself is always refused, and every name is checked to resolve inside the destination before anything is written. All timestamps are fixed, so extracting one archive twice produces the same tree and an AOT training run matches the production copy.

The source-containment check resolves the archive's real path and a destination that does not yet exist through its nearest existing ancestor, so symbolic-link and case aliases cannot hide the source. The check runs again immediately before publication. The standard Path API cannot make checking and replacement one indivisible operation, so a hostile process that can replace path components concurrently can still race it; source and destination directories must be writable only by trusted participants.

This class is loaded only when the mode selects it, so it is written in ordinary Java: the rules that keep io.micronaut.runner free of lambdas, streams and String.format do not apply to io.micronaut.runner.tools.

      Extracts the runner jar the launcher was started from.
      Parameters:
      args - the program arguments: "--destination" and "--force"
      archive - the runner jar
      index - the index read from it
      source - the archive's bytes, from which the nested jars are copied

      IOException - if the arguments are not understood, the destination cannot be used, the archive disagrees with its index, or a file cannot be written
